sources_considered.why: Read the published paper and its cost comparison. It tests misinformation generation and estimates its cost using non-OpenAI models.
Read to verify the study was already public in August 2024; the published paper supplies the evidence item.
Read the original cost analysis, but used the peer-reviewed version.
Read the abstract. Its modeled campaign economics address a broader cost boundary than marginal text generation.
The search result reports inexpensive generation using OpenAI itself; the selected study directly covers alternatives.

evidence_items.explanation: The experiments establish that alternatives can produce convincing election-disinformation content. For ten articles daily over a month, the cost section estimates $0.30 using Gemini or $9 using hosted Llama 3 70B, compared with $4,500 for the cited human-writing service; these are generation-stage estimates, not total campaign budgets.

unresolved_gaps: The study does not measure every cost of operating a real campaign.
It establishes a low marginal cost and an automation mechanism, not mathematical convergence to exactly zero.
